title: Intermittent fault: a conveyor stops at random 2-3 times a week, cause unknown
summary: A working investigation board for a conveyor that dies a few times a week — known facts separated hard from guesses.

blocks.eyebrow: Cause unknown — keep the ledger honest
blocks.title: Stops 2–3 times a week, no smoking gun
blocks.body: A packaging conveyor at a fictional plant halts without a clear pattern. This page is an investigation board: what is known stays known, what is guessed stays labeled as guess.

blocks.title: Rule for this page
blocks.body: Anything not observed, logged, or measured is a guess. Do not promote a guess into the Known column because it feels satisfying.

blocks.heading: KNOWN (verified)
rows: Conveyor stops 2–3 times per week
Maintenance log + operator reports, last 6 weeks
Restart often works after a minute
Operator statements; no formal MTTR study yet
No standing fault on the HMI when techs arrive
Multiple work orders say "cleared / no code"
E-stop circuit not latched when found stopped
Checked twice on different days
Motor nameplate and VFD size match the design print
Nameplate photo vs. print revision C
blocks.caption: If it is not on this table, it is not known yet.

blocks.heading: GUESSED (unverified hypotheses)
columns: What would confirm or kill it
rows: Flaky photoeye on the infeed
Trend the input bit; wiggle test; replace only after correlation
Overheat on a soft-start / VFD
Thermal camera during run; fault history download
Intermittent network loss to the PLC
Managed switch logs; watchdog timers; duplicate IP hunt
Mechanical bind when cold
Stops clustered on Monday mornings? Check timestamps before blaming temperature
Operator bumping a pull-cord
Camera or witness — do not assume people are the fault
blocks.caption: Guesses are useful. Mislabeling them as facts is how intermittent faults live forever.

blocks.heading: Next measurements (not next opinions)
items: Export VFD and PLC fault histories for the last 30 days — even "empty" is data.
Add a cheap datalogger or use existing historian on run permission, drive ready, and the two most-suspected inputs.
Require a photo of the HMI and the drive keypad before anyone resets — breaks the "no code" fog.
Only after correlation: change one thing, label the WO with the hypothesis ID from the Guessed table.

nodes.title: Field inputs
nodes.detail: Eyes, proxes, pull cords — vibration and loose connectors.

nodes.title: Drive / motor
nodes.detail: Thermal, DC bus, encoder (if any), wiring to the motor.

nodes.title: PLC & network
nodes.detail: Scan time, IO drops, switch errors — silent until you log them.

nodes.title: Mechanicals
nodes.detail: Seized roller, slipping clutch, jam that clears itself.

blocks.heading: How to talk about uncertainty on the floor

columns.name: Say this
columns.detail: "Known: stops ~3×/week with no retained fault. Guess: photoeye. Next: trend that bit for two weeks."

columns.name: Not this
columns.detail: "It's definitely the eye" after one glance, or "the PLC is haunted" with no logs.

columns.name: Why
columns.detail: Intermittents punish confident storytelling. They reward boring instrumentation.

items.label: Separate Known vs Guessed in the WO
Declare when a guess is retired
items.detail: Write "killed: cold bind — stops occur on warm Fridays too."

blocks.heading: Classification check
blocks.prompt: A tech says "I bet it's the network." Where does that belong on this board?
options: Known table — techs betting counts as verification
Guessed table — until logs or tests confirm
Neither — delete it so the board stays tidy
blocks.explanation: A bet is a hypothesis. It goes in Guessed with a confirmation test attached.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct — label it Guessed and add a kill/confirm test.
blocks.wrongFeedback: Re-read the page rule: unverified ideas stay in Guessed.

blocks.heading: Leave the board better than you found it
blocks.body: Update Known and Guessed after every stop. The cause is allowed to remain unknown until the data says otherwise.
